title: Existing account: pre-session check-in
summary: A deal already in the CRM, with budget, signer and next session recorded. The customer reconfirms two of them, adds a new stakeholder, and asks to move the session.
showcases: Corroboration: the budget and signer match the CRM, so nothing changes (NO_OP)
Deterministic overwrite protection: an explicit, agreed reschedule still goes to review because it would replace an existing CRM value
A new stakeholder is heard and kept, but isn't recorded as the decision maker

turns.text: Thanks for jumping on, Saoirse. I wanted to check in before Wednesday's session and see if anything has changed on your end.
A couple of things. The good news first: the $250K is still the approved budget for this rollout. Nothing has changed there.
Great to hear. And Lucian is still the one signing the agreement?
Yes, Lucian signs. One addition, though. Matthias Albrecht just joined as our IT director, and he'll be leading the technical evaluation from here.
Hi Gideon. I'll mostly be looking at security and data retention.
The other thing is Wednesday. Our quarterly close review landed on top of it. Could we move the session to Friday at 10 instead?
Friday at 10 works on our side. I'll update the invite.

budget.why: The customer explicitly reconfirms the approved $250K, which equals the CRM value. That's corroboration, not a write.

decisionMaker.why: "Yes, Lucian signs" reconfirms the CRM signer ("Lucian" matches "Lucian Ferro" under the frozen name rule). Matthias leads the technical evaluation, which is a supporting role (INDIRECT). Reconciliation sets him aside because a DIRECT signer survives.
risks: If the classifier labels Matthias DIRECT (a classification error), the two signers conflict and the field becomes ASK. That's safe, but not the intended demo.
If the extractor writes "Lucian Ferro" (from the CRM) instead of "Lucian", the result is the same NO_OP.

nextMeeting.why: The customer asks to move the session to Friday at 10, and the seller agrees: explicit, current and direct. The call is Monday 2026-11-16, so Friday is 2026-11-20 and "at 10" reads 10:00. Because the CRM already holds Wed 2026-11-18 10:00, policy rule 6 adds CONFLICTS_WITH_EXISTING: Grounded never overwrites autonomously. (This is the pattern the self-assessing baseline wrote automatically on TEST.)
risks: The extractor may also emit the old Wednesday session as a SUPERSEDED candidate. It's ABSTAIN and appears in the ledger; the field decision is unaffected.

dryRuns.label: Primary: extraction and labels as intended
